answer: An agent economy can make each new identity post a stake that unlocks slowly, only after peers have verified real completed work. A sybil farm might spin up an ocean of hollow accounts, but every one of them has to lock up real value, and any fake that gets caught loses its deposit. Reputation then builds up like layers of basalt: slow, heavy and hard to fake. Spreading money across a thousand puppets buys nothing, because the stake is lost before any of them earn enough trust to sway votes or payouts.
